candidates.source_name: Cyril of Alexandria / Commentary on Matthew
candidates.source_attribution: Cyril of Alexandria, Commentary on Matthew (fragments), preserved in J.A. Cramer, Catenae Graecorum Patrum in Novum Testamentum, Vol. I: In Evangelia S. Matthaei et S. Marci (Oxford: University Press, 1840). PD. Greek text also in PG 72 cols. 365-474.
candidates.draft_body:
Cyril of Alexandria Commentary on Matthew (c. 430 AD)

The Transfiguration on Tabor: Cyril sees the unveiled brightness as the Son's eternal glory momentarily disclosed to the apostolic three — uncreated because pre-temporal, the same light by which the Word is Light from Light. Tewahedo Buhe (Mäskäräm-Transfiguration feast, August 19 Julian / Päguemen 13 Geʿez) is among the great dominical feasts, the Cyrillian uncreated-light theology preserved in its Mäzämmǝr.

candidates.draft_body:
Cyril of Alexandria Commentary on Matthew (c. 430 AD)

'This is my beloved Son; hear ye him': Cyril sees the Father's voice completing the Mosaic-Elijah witness on Tabor — the Law (Moses) and the Prophets (Elijah) defer to the incarnate Son to whom they testified. The hearing-imperative inaugurates Christ-centered hermeneutics.
